title: Statistics and Probability — Understanding God's World
description: Test your understanding of statistics, probability, distributions, inference, and regression.

questions.question: Which sampling method gives every member of the population an equal chance of being selected?
questions.explanation: Simple random sampling gives every member of the population an equal chance of being selected, which helps ensure the sample is representative and minimizes selection bias.

questions.question: Which measure of center is most resistant to outliers?
questions.explanation: The median is resistant to outliers because it depends only on the middle value(s) when data is ordered, not on extreme values. The mean is pulled toward outliers.

questions.question: According to the empirical rule, approximately what percentage of data in a normal distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
questions.explanation: The empirical rule (68-95-99.7 rule) states that approximately 95% of data falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean in a normal distribution.

questions.question: What does a p-value measure in hypothesis testing?
options: The probability that the null hypothesis is true
The probability of observing data as extreme as the sample data if the null hypothesis is true
The probability that the alternative hypothesis is true
The probability of making a correct decision
questions.explanation: A p-value is the probability of obtaining results as extreme as (or more extreme than) the observed results, assuming the null hypothesis is true. It is NOT the probability that H₀ is true.

questions.question: What is a Type I error in hypothesis testing?
options: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis
Accepting the alternative hypothesis when there is no data
questions.explanation: A Type I error (false positive) occurs when we reject the null hypothesis when it is actually true — concluding there is an effect when there isn't one.

questions.question: If the correlation coefficient between two variables is r = -0.85, what can we conclude?
options: There is a strong positive linear relationship
There is a weak negative linear relationship
There is a strong negative linear relationship
One variable causes the other to decrease
questions.explanation: An r value of -0.85 indicates a strong negative linear relationship — as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease. However, correlation does not imply causation.

questions.question: The Central Limit Theorem states that as sample size increases, the distribution of sample means approaches what shape?
questions.explanation: The Central Limit Theorem states that the distribution of sample means approaches a normal distribution as sample size increases, regardless of the shape of the population distribution.

questions.question: In a binomial distribution with n = 20 trials and p = 0.3, what is the expected number of successes (mean)?
questions.explanation: The mean of a binomial distribution is μ = np = 20 × 0.3 = 6. On average, we expect 6 successes in 20 trials when the probability of success is 0.3.

questions.question: Why is extrapolation (predicting beyond the range of observed data) generally unreliable?
options: The correlation always becomes weaker outside the data range
We have no evidence that the pattern continues beyond the observed range
It violates the Central Limit Theorem
questions.explanation: Extrapolation is unreliable because we have no data to support the assumption that the observed pattern (linear or otherwise) continues beyond the range of our observations.

questions.question: Which Biblical principle most directly supports the importance of testing claims with evidence before accepting them?
options: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the Lord
Test everything; hold fast what is good
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:21 — 'Test everything; hold fast what is good' — directly supports the principle of hypothesis testing: evaluating claims with evidence before drawing conclusions.
